lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text: Hello! Today we are learning about families, and I am so happy to do this with you. This page is called The Lesson. It has 7 short parts about your family. We will read them slowly, one by one. By the end, you will be able to say who is in your family and one thing your family taught you. You need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. Take your time — there's no rush. Here is what to do, step by step. 1. Start at the top of the page with part 1, Who is in my family. Read it slowly with your grown-up. Then press the button that says Listen to this part, and listen while it is read to you. It is good to listen and follow the words at the same time. 2. When part 1 is done, say one thing you learned from it, out loud to me or to your grown-up. A good answer is a full sentence, like "I learned that my family has four people." Just one thing is perfect. I will listen and tell you what I liked about your answer. 3. Now go to part 2, What do I call them. Read it, then press Listen to this part again. This part has the special names, like Hooyo and Aabo and Ayeeyo. Try saying those names out loud. Then tell me one thing you learned. 4. Next is part 3, What do we do together. Read it and press Listen to this part. This part has little boxes about eating, playing and singing together. Think about which ones your family does. Then say one thing you learned. 5. Now part 4, What does my family teach me. Read it, press Listen to this part, and think about who taught you things. Can you wash your hands? Who showed you how? Then tell me one thing you learned. 6. Next is part 5, I say thank you. Read it and press Listen to this part. Think of one way you help at home, like tidying a toy. Then say one thing you learned. 7. Now part 6, Ask an older person. Read it and press Listen to this part. This part gives you questions for Ayeeyo or Awoowe. Pick your favourite question. Then tell me one thing you learned. 8. Last is part 7, Before you go. Read it and press Listen to this part. It asks you three easy questions about your family. Answer them out loud to your grown-up. Then say one thing you learned. 9. When all 7 parts are done, scroll to the bottom. Press the button that says I have read the lesson. Only press it when you have really read every part, because that is how the page knows you finished. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read the lesson at the bottom. Then your work is saved and you are done! Now let's start with something small. Read part 1 and press Listen to this part. Tell me when you are ready. 🙂

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 1. The big question is: What can families teach us? This page is our first look at the unit. It tells us what we will learn. We do this so you know where we are going, like looking at a map before a walk. You need your ears, your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. There are three little steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Look at the words on the screen. Then press the button that says Listen to the overview. Sit still and listen all the way to the end. Try to catch one word about families. I expect you to listen quietly, right to the end. Step 2. Now say it back in your own words. You can say it to me or to your grown-up. A good answer is one or two sentences, like "This unit is about my family and what they teach me." I expect you to use your own words, not copy the screen. Say it out loud, nice and clear. Step 3. Press the button at the bottom that says I have read the overview. Only press it after you have listened and talked. That button tells us you are ready. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read the overview. Then we can go on to the first lesson: Who is in my family? Go ahead and press Listen to the overview now. Tell me when you are done! 🙂

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text:
Hello! Let's get this page done together. 🙂

This page is called My Learning Goals. It shows what we will learn in Unit 1: What can families teach us? We read our goals first, so we know where we are going. It is like looking at a map before a walk. You need your voice, your eyes, and a grown-up sitting beside you. Here is what I expect from you: point with your finger, read out loud with your grown-up, and talk in full sentences. There are no marks here. Talking well is the win. There are 3 steps. Here they all are. 1. Read My Learning Goals. Look at the list on your screen. With your grown-up, read each goal out loud, one at a time. Point at each goal with your finger as you read it. Our goals are these: say who is in my family; say the special names we call them, like Hooyo and Ayeeyo; talk about what we do together; notice what my family teaches me; say thank you; and ask an older person about when they were little. Do it well by going slowly and reading every one. I expect you to read them all, not just the first one. 2. Say each goal in your own words. Now close your mouth for a second and think. Then say each goal again, but in YOUR words, not the words on the screen. For example, you could say, "I will tell about the people in my home." A good answer starts with "I will..." After that, tell your grown-up which goal you think will be the hardest for you, and say why. Try to give one reason, like "because I get shy." I expect one sentence for each goal, and one hardest goal with a reason. 3. Press the Done button. When you have read the goals and said them your own way, look at the bottom of the page. Find the button that says Done. Press it. Only press it after you have really talked, because that button saves your good work. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Done, and you can tell your grown-up what this unit is about. Now go and do step 1. When you have read the goals, come back and tell me which goal sounds most fun to you!

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text:
Hello! Today you are going to make something lovely: a My Family poster. This is your mini-project. We do it because it shows everything you learned in this unit, all in one happy picture. By the end, you will be able to point at your poster and tell someone about your family. You will need one big sheet of paper, crayons or coloured pencils, and your grown-up sitting with you. Glue and a photo are nice too, but not needed. Here is what I expect from you: draw with care, say the names out loud, and be proud. Neat is not the goal. Talking about your family is the goal. 🙂

There are three things to do on this page. 1. Read the Mini-Project first. Look at the page and let your grown-up read it out loud to you. Listen for what you will make and how many steps there are. There are five little steps in the project. Do not draw yet. Just listen and picture it in your head. I expect you to be able to say, "I am making a family poster."

2. Now do the five steps, one at a time. Do not rush ahead. Finish one step, then start the next. Step one: draw the people you love. Put them in the middle of your big paper. Draw everyone who lives with you, and people like Ayeeyo or Awoowe too. A pet can go in as well. Give everyone a big smile. Big family or small family, both are just right. Step two: add their names. Point to each person and say their name out loud. Your grown-up can help you write the name under each one. I expect to hear you say every name, not just point. Step three: add one thing your family taught you. Pick just one. It could be washing your hands, counting to ten, saying hello, or helping at home. Draw that one thing on your poster. Step four: make it beautiful. Add colours, hearts, flowers, or the sun. At the top, your grown-up can help you write the title: My Family. Step five: show and tell. Show your poster to someone you love. Finish these out loud: "This is my family. This is..." then "My family taught me to..." then "I love my family because..." Say them in a big, clear voice. 3. Press the Done button at the bottom. Only press it when your poster is finished and you have told someone about it. That button saves your good work, so it must come from you. You will know the page is finished when your poster has your family, their names, one thing they taught you, a title, and you pressed Done. Now go and do step one. When your drawing is ready, come back and tell me who you drew!

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text: Well done for getting all the way to the last page! This one is called Reflection. Reflection means looking back at your learning and thinking about how it went. We do it because it helps you see what you are good at, and what you still want help with. By the end, you will have thought about your own learning all by yourself. You need your eyes, your voice, and your grown-up sitting beside you. Here is what I expect from you: read each sentence with your grown-up, think for a moment, and pick the answer that is true for YOU. There is no right or wrong here. Take your time — there's no rush. There are 4 steps. Here they all are. 1. Look at the sentences at the top of the page. Your grown-up reads one sentence out loud. It will be about how you learn, like drawing or talking about your family. Then you choose the answer that fits you. You might choose Great, or Good, or Not sure yet. Say your answer out loud first, then tap it. Do this for every sentence on the page. 2. Be honest. This is the most important part! If something was easy, say it was easy. If something was tricky, choose Not sure yet. That is a brave, good answer. It shows your teacher where to help you next time. Nobody gets a mark, and nobody will be cross. Honest is always best. 3. Now look under the sentences. There is a little slide deck there, with one sentence on each slide. Press Start to begin. Read the sentence with your grown-up, choose your answer, then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going, one slide at a time. On the last slide, press the finish button. 4. When every single sentence has an answer, press the button at the bottom that says I have finished reflecting. Check first that you did not skip any. If one is empty, go back and choose an answer for it, then press the button. You will know the page is done when every sentence has an answer and you have pressed I have finished reflecting. Then your whole unit about families is complete! Off you go with step 1. Tell me when you have done it, and I will check it with you. 🙂

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text: Hello! Let's get you ready for your live teacher session. This page tells you what to bring and what you will talk about with your teacher and the other children. We do this so you feel happy and ready, not shy. By the end, you will know exactly what to say about your family. You need your family drawing, a grown-up next to you, and your talking voice. There are three things to do on this page. Here they all are. 1. Read the Teacher Session part. Ask your grown-up to read it out loud with you. Look at what to bring, like your family drawing or a photo. Look at the questions you will talk about, such as who is in your family and one thing your family taught you. I expect you to listen carefully and put your drawing right next to you, ready. 2. Say your answers out loud now. Do not just think them in your head. Say them to your grown-up, like this: "This is my family. This is my Hooyo." Then say one thing your family taught you, like "My family taught me to wash my hands." A good answer says a name and a whole sentence. I expect you to say every answer out loud at least one time, in a big, brave voice. 3. Press the Done button at the bottom. Only press it after you have read the page and said your answers. That button tells us you are ready. I expect you to press it yourself, with your grown-up watching. You will know the page is finished when you have read it, said your answers out loud, and pressed Done. Now try step one, and tell me when you have read it. Take your time — there's no rush.

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 2. The big question is: What kind of garden would be best? This page is our welcome page. It tells us what our garden unit is about. We do it so you know where we are going, like looking at a map before a walk. You will need your ears, your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. There are three small steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Read the unit overview. Look at the words at the top of the page. Then press Listen to the overview. That button reads the words out loud to you. Sit still and listen right to the end. I expect you to hear two things: the big question about gardens, and the fun jobs you will do, like drawing, sorting and planting. Step 2. Say in your own words what the unit is about. Turn to your grown-up and tell them. You can start like this: "This unit is about gardens. I will..." A good answer names gardens and one thing you will do, like plant a seed or draw a garden. It does not need to be long. Your own words are the best words. Step 3. Press I have read the overview at the bottom. Scroll down to the bottom of the page. Find the button that says I have read the overview and press it. Only press it after you have listened and talked. That press tells the page you are ready. You will know the page is finished when you have listened, said what the unit is about, and pressed I have read the overview. Now go and do Step 1. Press Listen to the overview, then come back and tell me one thing you heard. 🌱

lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text:
Hello! I am your teacher today, and I am so glad you are here. 🌱

This page is called The Lesson. It has 7 little parts about gardens. We read them one at a time, and you can hear them read out loud too. By the end, you will know what grows in a garden and what a plant needs to grow. Get a pencil, some paper, and a grown-up to sit with you. Here is our whole plan, step by step. 1. Get ready. Sit somewhere comfy with your paper and pencil. Turn your sound on, so you can hear the voice read to you. I expect you to be ready to look, point and talk. 2. Start with Part 1, "Look at the garden". Read it slowly. Then press Listen to this part and hear it again. Point at each word as you listen. That is how we read like a big learner. 3. After Part 1, tell me one thing you learned. Just one thing, out loud or typed to me. A good answer sounds like this: "I learned that a garden can have a butterfly in it." I expect one real thing you noticed, not "I don't know". 4. Now do the same for every other part. Read it, press Listen to this part, then say one thing you learned. The parts are: Part 2, draw a garden. Part 3, what grows in a garden. Part 4, what do plants need. Part 5, which garden do you like best. Part 6, count the seeds. Part 7, before you go. 5. Do the little jobs inside the parts too. In Part 2 you draw a garden. In Part 3 you sort plants into "eat it" or "look at it". In Part 4 you tick the things a plant needs. In Part 5 you pick your favourite garden and say why. In Part 6 you count seeds. Doing them makes the lesson stick in your head. 6. Take your time. There is no rush. You can do a few parts today and the rest another day. If a part feels tricky, tell me and I will help you with a small hint. 7. Last of all, press I have read the lesson at the bottom. Only press it when you have read all 7 parts. That button tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you have read every part, said one thing from each part, and pressed I have read the lesson. Ready? Let's start with Part 1. Read it, press Listen to this part, then tell me one thing you saw in the garden.

bigideas.label: Big Ideas
bigideas.text:
Hello! Today we are on the Big Ideas page. Big Ideas are the most important things to remember from our garden unit. This one is called "Look after your seed." By the end, you will know how to care for a little plant. You just need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. There are three steps. Let's start with something small. Step 1. Read each Big Idea, then press the Listen button next to it. Listen carefully all the way to the end. You can press Listen again if you want to hear it twice. I expect you to look at the words while you listen. That helps your ears and your eyes work together. Step 2. Now say what the idea means in your own words. Do not copy the words on the screen — use your own! Then give one example from your own life. For example, you might say: "It means give my plant a little water, like when I water Mum's flowers." A good answer has two parts: what it means, and your own example. Say it out loud to your grown-up, then tell me too. Step 3. When you have read and listened to every Big Idea, press the Done button at the bottom of the page. Press it only after you have finished them all. That button saves your good work. You will know the page is finished when every Big Idea has been listened to, you have said each one in your own words, and the Done button is pressed. Then you are all set! 🌱

Ready to press Listen on the first one?

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text: Hello! Today we start our Mini-Project. This is the fun one! In this project you will grow a real plant, or draw your best garden. You can do both if you like. We do this to find out what plants need, and to choose the garden you like best. By the end, you will show your work to someone and tell them about it. You will need a grown-up next to you, a cup, some soil, a seed, and crayons and paper. Here is our whole plan. Read it with your grown-up. 1. Read the Mini-Project. First, let your grown-up read the Mini-Project box out loud to you. Look at the pictures as you listen. This tells you what you will make and how. I expect you to listen and then say one thing out loud: "I will plant a seed" or "I will draw a garden" or "I will do both." That is your choice, and it is a good one. 2. Choice A — Plant a seed. Get a cup, some soil, and a seed. A bean seed is a good one. Fill the cup with soil, almost to the top. Push the seed in, not too deep, and cover it gently. Give it a small drink of water. Put the cup on a sunny windowsill. I expect gentle hands and just a little water — not too much! 3. Look after your seed each day. Give it a tiny drink of water every day. Look at the soil and see what is new. Be patient. A seed sleeps for a few days before it wakes up. One day a tiny green shoot will push up. That is so exciting! When it grows, draw your plant in the box. 4. Choice B — Make your garden plan. Talk with your grown-up and answer three things: what you will grow, what you will do in the garden, and one creature you hope will visit. You can say the answers or draw them. I expect a reason too, like "I will grow tomatoes because I like to eat them." Strong opinions need strong reasons! 5. Choice B — Draw your best garden. In the big box, draw your garden. Draw the plants and the flowers. You can draw yourself in it too. You can add a bench to sit on, or a little path to walk on. I expect lots of colour and lots of ideas. There is no wrong garden — it is yours. 6. Show and tell. Show your plant or your picture to your family or your class. Tell them three things: what you grew or drew, why you like it, and what a plant needs to grow. Remember the three things: sun, water and soil. I expect a big, clear voice, and I expect you to look at the person you are telling. 7. Press Done. When your project is finished, scroll to the bottom of the page and press the Done button. That saves your work. Only you can press it — I cannot do that part for you! You will know the page is finished when you have planted your seed or drawn your garden, told someone about it, and pressed Done. Now let's start with step 1. Read the Mini-Project with your grown-up, then tell me: will you plant a seed, draw a garden, or do both?

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 2. Our big question is: what kind of garden would be best? This page is called My Learning Goals. A goal is something you are trying to do. This page tells you what you will learn in this unit. We read it first so you know where we are going. It is like looking at a map before a walk. You will need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up to read with you. There are three things to do. Here they all are. 1. Read My Learning Goals. Look at the top of your screen. Your grown-up can read each goal out loud, slowly. Point at each one with your finger as you hear it. The goals are about gardens: looking at a garden, drawing a garden, finding out what grows there, finding out what plants need, choosing the garden you like best, and counting seeds. I expect you to listen to every goal and point at each one. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Say each goal in your own words. Now it is your turn to talk. For each goal, say it your own way. Like this: "I will look at a garden." Or: "I will find out what plants need." You do not need the same words as the page. Your words are perfect. Then tell your grown-up, or tell me, which goal you think will be the hardest for you. Say why, too. Try to use the word "because" — like "That one is hard because I have never planted a seed." I expect one sentence for each goal, and one hardest goal with a reason. 3. Press the Done button. When you have said all the goals out loud, look at the bottom of the page. Find the button that says Done. Press it. That tells the page you have finished. Only press it after you have talked about the goals — that way your work is really yours. You will know the page is finished when you have read the goals, said them in your own words, picked your hardest one, and pressed Done. Then we can go and look at a real garden together! Which goal do you think sounds the most fun? 🌱

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text: Well done for getting all the way to the end of our garden unit! This last page is called Reflection. Reflecting means looking back and thinking about how your learning went. You will read some sentences about yourself, and pick the answer that is true for you. You need your grown-up to read with you, and your honest thinking. There are four small steps. Here they all are. 1. First, look at the sentences at the top of the page. Your grown-up reads one sentence out loud, like "I know a plant needs sun, water and soil." Think about it for a moment. Then choose the answer that feels true for you. I expect you to think before you choose, not just tap fast. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Now the most important rule: be honest. There are no marks here, and nothing is wrong. If you say "not yet" for something, that is a good, brave answer! It tells your teacher which part to help you with next time. So pick "great" only when you really can do it, and pick "not yet" when you still need help. 3. Next, go down to the slides at the bottom of the page. There is one sentence on each slide. Press Start to begin. Read the sentence with your grown-up, choose your answer, then press the arrow to go to the next one. Keep going, one sentence at a time. On the last slide, press the finish button. I expect every slide to have an answer, with no slide skipped. 4. Last, press I have finished reflecting at the bottom of the page. Only press it when every sentence has an answer. That button saves your thinking, so it must be you who presses it, not me. You will know the page is finished when the slides are all done and the I have finished reflecting button has been pressed. Then this unit is complete! Before you start, tell me one thing: what was the best part of the garden project for you? 🌱

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text: Hello! Today we are getting ready for your live Teacher Session. A live session is when you meet your teacher and friends on the screen. You will talk about gardens together. This page tells you what to bring and what you will talk about. Reading it first means you will feel ready and happy, not shy. All you need is your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up nearby. There are 3 steps. Here they are. Step 1. Read the Teacher Session page with your grown-up. Ask them to read each line out loud, slowly. Look for two things: what to bring, and the questions you will talk about. Bring things like your garden drawing, your seed in the cup, and a crayon. The questions may be ones like "What can people do in a garden?" and "What does a plant need to grow?" I expect you to point at each thing on the page as your grown-up reads it. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 2. Now say your answers out loud, right now. Do not just think them. Say them in a full sentence, like "A plant needs sun, water and soil." For the garden question you can say "In a garden people can dig, plant seeds and water the plants." Say why you like something too: "I like the flower garden because butterflies come." I expect one clear sentence for each question, said in a big, brave voice. Practising now makes talking in the live session easy. Step 3. Press the Done button at the bottom of the page. Press it only after you have read everything and said your answers out loud. That button tells your teacher you are ready. I cannot press it for you — that part is your job. You will know the page is finished when you have read it, said your answers out loud, and the Done button is pressed. Shall we start with Step 1? Tell me when you have read the page. 🌱

lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this page is called The Lesson. It is all about jobs — the work people do. By the end, you will be able to name some jobs, say who helps us, and tell me the job you would like to do. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a grown-up sitting with you. Let's start! 1. Look at the top of the page. The Lesson has 7 parts. Part 1 is "Jobs I can see". Read it slowly with your grown-up, then press Listen to this part to hear it read out loud. Listening and reading together helps the words stick. 2. Now tell me one thing you learned from Part 1. Just one small sentence is perfect, like "A farmer grows food." You can say it out loud to your grown-up, or type it here to me. I would love to hear it! 3. Go to Part 2, "Who helps us? Match them". Read it, then press Listen to this part again. This part has a table of helpers. Point to each helper and say how they help us. 4. Tell me one thing you learned from Part 2. Try to name one helper and how they help. For example: "A tailor makes our clothes."

5. Now Part 3, "Match the worker to the tool". Read it and press Listen to this part. A tool is a thing a worker uses. Point at each worker and say which tool they use. Then tell me one thing you learned. 6. Next is Part 4, "Girls and boys can do any job". Read it and press Listen to this part. This one is important, so read it slowly. Then tell me one thing you learned from it. 7. Part 5 is "Ask a grown-up about their job". Read it and press Listen to this part. Ask your grown-up the three questions on the page. Then tell me one thing you found out. 8. Part 6 is "The job I would like". Read it and press Listen to this part. Think quietly: what job would you like when you grow up? Tell me the job and one tool you would use. 9. The last part is "Before you go". Read it and press Listen to this part. Answer the three questions out loud with your grown-up. Then tell me one thing you learned. 10. When you have read all 7 parts, press I have read the lesson at the bottom of the page. That button tells the page you are done. When you have pressed it, the page is finished — and you can come back and tell me! Take your time — there's no rush. Ready? Start with Part 1 and press Listen to this part. 🙂

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 3. The big question is: What do we know about jobs? A job is the work a person does. In this unit you will look at jobs, meet people who help us, and dream about the job you would like. This page is just the start — it tells you what is coming. You need your eyes, your ears, and your talking voice. A grown-up can sit with you. Here are the three things to do on this page. 1. Read the unit overview. Press the button that says Listen to the overview. Then sit still and listen all the way to the end. Try to hear the name Leila — she is the girl from Ehel Academy who loves to watch people at work. I expect you to listen right to the end, not press stop early. 2. Say in your own words what the unit is about. Tell your grown-up, or type it to me. You do not need long words. Something like "this unit is about jobs people do" is perfect. I expect one or two sentences from you, in YOUR words, not the same words as the page. 3. Press I have read the overview. This button is at the bottom of the page. Only press it after you have listened and talked. That press tells the page you are ready. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read the overview at the bottom. Then we move on to Jobs I can see. Let's start with step 1. Press Listen to the overview now, and tell me when it has finished. 🙂

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 3: What do we know about jobs? This page is called My Learning Goals. A goal is something you are trying to learn. We look at our goals first, so you know where we are going. It is like looking at a map before a walk. You will need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up to read with you. There are three small steps. Step 1. Read My Learning Goals. Look at the list on your screen. Ask your grown-up to read each goal out loud, slowly. The goals are things like: I can name some jobs people do. I can say how one person helps us. I can draw the job I would like to do. I can show my picture and listen to others. I expect you to listen to every goal and point at each one as it is read. That is all — no writing yet. Step 2. Say each goal in your own words. Now it is your turn to talk. After each goal, say it back in YOUR words. For example, you could say, "I will learn the names of lots of jobs." A good answer uses your own words, not the same words on the page. Then tell your grown-up which goal you think will be the hardest for you, and say why. I expect one reason, even a tiny one, like "because I do not know many jobs yet." There is no wrong answer here. Step 3. Press the Done button. When you have talked about all the goals, find the Done button at the bottom of the page. Press it once. This tells the page that you have finished looking at your goals. You will know the page is finished when you have said every goal in your own words, told your grown-up your hardest one, and pressed Done. Off you go with Step 1. When you have listened to all the goals, come back and tell me. 🙂

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this is our Mini-Project. A mini-project means one big fun piece of work. You will draw the job you would like to do when you grow up. Then you will show it and talk about it. We do this because it helps you name jobs, think about tools, and speak in a proud voice. You will need paper, crayons or coloured pencils, and a grown-up close by. Take your time — there is no rush. Here is everything, step by step. 1. Read the Mini-Project. Look at the page on your screen. Ask your grown-up to read it out loud to you. Point at each part as they read. I expect you to listen and look, and then tell your grown-up one thing you will make. The answer is: a picture of me doing a job! 2. Think of a job. Close your eyes. What job would you like when you grow up? A doctor? A farmer? A pilot? A teacher? A fisher? Pick the one you like best. I expect one job, and a reason. Try saying: "I would like to be a ... because ..."

3. Talk about your job. Before you draw, talk with your grown-up. What would you do in this job? What tools would you use? What clothes would you wear? Where would you work? I expect you to answer all four out loud. Remember: a tool is a thing a worker uses, like a needle or a hoe. 4. Draw yourself doing the job. Now draw! Put yourself in the picture, doing the work. Draw your tools too, and your special clothes. Use lots of colours. A good drawing shows me the job even before you tell me. Wobbly lines are fine — proud work is the best work. 5. Give your picture a name. Ask your grown-up to write at the top: I would like to be a ... and then your job. I expect the words to be at the top, so everyone can read them first. 6. Show and tell. Show your picture to your family or your class. Tell them four things: what job you would like, what you would do, what you would use, and why you like it. Speak in a big, proud voice. Look at the people you are telling. And listen when it is their turn. 7. Make a jobs display (if you are with a class). Put all the pictures together on a big wall. Look at them all. Can you see girls and boys doing every kind of job? Anyone can do any job! 8. Press Done. When your project is finished, go to the bottom of the page and press the Done button. I cannot press it for you — only you can, because it is your work. You will know the page is finished when your picture is drawn, you have shown it and talked about it, and the Done button is pressed. 🌟

Now tell me: what job have you chosen?

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text: Hello! This is our Reflection page. Reflection means looking back at what we did. We are doing it to think about the jobs we learned, and to say what we liked and what still feels tricky. There is nothing to get right or wrong here. All you need is your voice, your grown-up next to you, and your honest thinking. Here are the steps, one at a time. 1. Read the sentences. On the page you will see sentences about how you learn, like "I can name some jobs people do." Ask your grown-up to read each one out loud to you. Think about it for a moment. Then choose the answer that is true for you. Some pages use faces: Great, Good, or Not sure yet. Pick the one that matches how you feel. I expect you to think before you tap, not just tap fast. 2. Be honest. This is the most important part. If a sentence feels easy, say so. If it feels hard, say that too! Picking "Not sure yet" is not naughty. It tells your teacher exactly where to help you next. I expect brave, true answers, even when the true answer is "not yet". 3. Do the slides at the bottom. Under the sentences there is a little deck of slides. Each slide has one sentence. Press Start to begin. Read the sentence with your grown-up, choose your answer, then press the arrow to go to the next one. Keep going, one slide at a time. On the last slide, press the finish button. Take your time — there is no rush. 4. Press I have finished reflecting. When every sentence has an answer, press the button at the bottom that says I have finished reflecting. Make sure nothing is left blank first. Give the page one last look with your grown-up. You will know the page is done when every sentence has your answer, the slides are finished, and you have pressed I have finished reflecting. Now, tell me your first thought: what did you like best in this jobs unit? 🙂

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text: Hello! Today we are getting you ready for your live teacher session. That is the class where you meet your teacher and other learners and talk about jobs. On this page you read what to bring and the questions you will talk about. Then you say your answers out loud, so your voice is ready. You need your jobs drawing, a grown-up nearby, and a big, proud voice. There are three steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Read the Teacher Session page with your grown-up. Look at the "Before we start" part first. It says three kind things: there are no wrong dreams, a girl can be anything and a boy can be anything, and we take turns and listen. Then read the questions you will talk about, like "What is your favourite job now? Why?" and "Who is a person that helps our town?" I expect you to point at each question as your grown-up reads it. Do not just look at the page — listen and think. Step 2. Now say your answers out loud, right now, before the class. Take your time — there's no rush. A good answer has two parts: the job, and a reason. Like this: "I would like to be a fisher, because I like boats." Try to say a full sentence, not just one word. Also get your drawing ready, so you can hold it up and show it. Say each answer one time, then say it again a bit louder. Step 3. When you have read the page and said your answers out loud, press the Done button at the bottom. Only press it after you have really practised. Pressing Done is how the page saves your good work. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Done and it stops waiting for you. Brilliant work! Now tell me one thing: what job will you talk about in your live session?

lesson.label: The Lesson
lesson.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for The Lesson page about water. This page has 6 short parts. We will read each one, listen to it, and then you say one thing you learned. By the end, you will know how we use water, why water is precious, and one way to save it. You need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. Let's start with something small. 1. Get ready. Sit with your grown-up and look at the top of the page. Find the button that says Listen to this part. You will press that button in every part. I expect you to sit comfy and be ready to listen carefully. 2. Part 1: Where do we use water? Read it slowly, then press Listen to this part and hear it again. It shows ways we use water, like drinking, washing hands, and watering plants. Tick the boxes for the ways you use water at home, then count your ticks. Now tell me one thing you learned, like "I use water to brush my teeth."

3. Part 2: Water is precious. Read it, then press Listen to this part. Precious means very special. Point to the child, the goat and the plant, and say "You need water!" out loud. Then tell me one thing you learned, in your own words. 4. Part 3: Save or waste? Read it, then press Listen to this part. For each line, say "save!" with a thumbs up, or "waste!" with a thumbs down. A good answer means you thought about it before your thumb moved. Then tell me one thing you learned. 5. Part 4: Count the drips. Read it, then press Listen to this part. Count the drips out loud and hold up that many fingers. Slow counting is best counting. Then tell me one thing you learned about a dripping tap. 6. Part 5: Draw a way to save water. Read it, then press Listen to this part. Draw yourself saving water in the box, big and bright. Then say to your grown-up: "I can save water by ..." and finish the sentence. Tell me one thing you learned from your drawing. 7. Part 6: Before you go. Read it, then press Listen to this part. Answer the three questions out loud with your grown-up. Full sentences make me smile! Then tell me one thing you learned from this last part. 8. Finish the page. When you have read and listened to all 6 parts, scroll to the bottom. Press I have read the lesson. Press it only when every part is really done. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read the lesson at the bottom, and you have said one thing you learned after each of the 6 parts. Take your time — there's no rush. Tell me when Part 1 is done, and I will be right here. 💧

goals.label: My Learning Goals
goals.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this page is called My Learning Goals. Learning goals are the things you will be able to do by the end of this unit. This unit asks a big question: How can we save water? Reading your goals first is like looking at a map before a walk. Then you know where we are going! Here is what I expect from you. Sit with your grown-up. Read slowly. Talk out loud. There are no wrong answers on this page. There are three steps. 1. Read My Learning Goals. Look at the list on your screen. Ask your grown-up to read each goal with you, one at a time. Point at each goal with your finger as you read it. Your goals in this unit are things like naming a way we use water, knowing that people, animals and plants all need water, saying one way to save water, and sharing your poster or your promise. Read them all before you go on. 2. Say each goal in your own words. Now close your eyes for a second and think. Then say each goal again, but in YOUR words, out loud to your grown-up. For example, you might say, "I will learn how water helps us." A good try is a short sentence that you understand. After that, point to the one goal you think will be the hardest for you, and say why. Saying "this one looks tricky" is brave and clever — it helps me help you. 3. Press the Done button. When you have read the goals and said them out loud, look at the bottom of the page. Press the Done button. That tells the page you have finished this part. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Done and the page lets you move on. Then you are ready for our first lesson about water. Which goal do you think will be the hardest one for you? Tell me, and we will make it easier together. 💧

overview.label: Unit Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 4. The big question is: How can we save water? This page is the front door of our unit. It tells you what we will learn together. We will find out where we use water, why water is precious, and how we can save it. Precious means very special. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a grown-up sitting near you. There are three little steps. Here they are. Step 1. Read the unit overview at the top of the page. It tells you the big question and what you will learn. Then press the button that says Listen to the overview. Sit still and listen all the way to the end. You will hear about Zane. He goes to Ehel Academy in Hargeisa, and he loves water. Listening right to the end is doing this step well. Step 2. Now say in your own words what this unit is about. Just talk out loud to your grown-up. You do not need to write. You could start like this: "This unit is about water and how I can save it." One or two sentences is plenty. I expect your own words, not the same words from the page. That is how I know your brain is thinking! Step 3. Last, press the button at the bottom that says I have read the overview. Only press it after you have listened and talked. That button tells the page you are ready. Do not press it early — finish steps one and two first. You will know the page is finished when you have listened to the overview, said in your own words what the unit is about, and pressed I have read the overview. Then the next page will be waiting for you. Ready? Start with Step 1, and tell me when you have listened. 💧

bigideas.label: Big Ideas
bigideas.text: Hello! Today we are on the Big Ideas page. Big Ideas are the most important thoughts in our water unit. There are two of them here: one about counting drips from a tap, and one called "Our water promise". By the end, you will be able to say what each big idea means in your own words. You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up sitting next to you. Let's start! 1. Read and listen. Look at the first Big Idea on your screen. Read it with your grown-up. Then press the Listen button for that idea. Sit still and listen all the way to the end. Then do the same for the second Big Idea. I expect you to press Listen for every idea, not just one. 2. Say it in your own words, and give an example. After each idea, tell your grown-up what it means, using your own words. Then say one thing from your own life. For the drips idea, you could say: "A dripping tap wastes water. My tap in the kitchen drips a little." For the water promise, you could say: "I promise to turn off the tap. I do that when I brush my teeth." A good answer has two parts: what it means, and something real from your day. 3. Press Done. When you have read both ideas, listened to both, and talked about both, scroll to the bottom. Press the Done button. Only press it when you have really finished them all — that button tells us your work is saved. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Listen on both ideas, said both in your own words, and pressed Done at the bottom. You did well today, water helper! Now tell me one thing: which Big Idea did you like best? 💧

project.label: Mini-Project
project.text:
Hello! Today you are the water helper. This page is your Mini-Project. You will make a water-saving poster, or say a water promise, and share it. We do this so you can tell other people how to look after water. Get your paper, your crayons, and your grown-up. I expect you to try your best, talk out loud, and have fun. Here is everything we will do. 1. Read the Mini-Project first. Sit with your grown-up and read the page together, from the top. It tells you what you will make and the steps to make it. Point at each part with your finger as you read. I expect you to know one thing before we start: are you making a poster, or saying a promise, or both? 2. Now do the steps in order, one at a time. Do not jump ahead. Finish one step, then go to the next. There are five little steps on the page. First, choose your best way to save water. Say it out loud to your grown-up, like "I can save water by turning off the tap."
Second, draw your poster in the box. Make it big and bright. You can draw yourself in it, smiling. Third, add your words at the top in big letters. Your grown-up can help you write them. Big letters are easy to read. Fourth, stand up tall and say your promise: "I promise to save water. I will ..." Say it clearly, with a big smile. Fifth, share it with your family or your class. Show your poster and tell them one way they can save water too. You can finish with the water chant and clap. 3. When your project is all finished, press the Done button at the bottom of the page. Only press it after you have drawn, spoken, and shared. Pressing Done saves your good work. You will know the page is finished when your poster is drawn, your promise is said out loud, and you have pressed Done. Ready? Start with step 1 and read the page with your grown-up. Then tell me your best water-saving idea. 💧

teacher.label: Teacher Session
teacher.text: Hello! Today we are getting ready for your live water lesson. In a live session, you meet your teacher and other children on the screen. You will talk about water together. Getting ready first makes you feel brave and happy. You need your eyes for reading with a grown-up, and your voice for talking. There are three steps. Here they all are. Step 1: Read the page with your grown-up. Look at the list of what to bring. It may be things like your drawing, a pencil, or your water poster. Then read the questions you will talk about. They will be water questions, like "What is one way you use water?" I expect you to point to each thing on the list and say it out loud. Great question! is what I say when you ask about a word you do not know — so ask your grown-up too. Step 2: Say your answers out loud, right now. Do not just think them — say them! For "How do we use water?" you could say "I use water to wash my hands." For "Why is water precious?" you could say "Because people, animals and plants all need water." For "How can I save water?" you could say "I turn the tap off when I brush my teeth." A good answer is one full sentence, said clearly and slowly. Say each one twice, so your mouth remembers it. Step 3: Press the Done button at the bottom of the page. Only press it after you have read the page and said your answers out loud. That button tells us you are ready for your live session. It saves your good work. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Done and the page shows it is complete. Then you are all set! Now, shall we start with Step 1? Tell me one thing you see on the "what to bring" list. 💧

reflect.label: Reflection
reflect.text: Well done for getting all the way to the end of our water unit! This last page is called Reflection. Reflection means looking back at your own learning. You will read some sentences about what you can do now, and choose the answer that is true for you. You need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up sitting with you. Here is the whole page, step by step. Step one. Look at the sentences near the top of the page. A grown-up can read each one out loud with you. They say things like "I can say one way to save water." For each one, choose the answer that is true for YOU. Think for a moment before you tap. I expect you to think about our water walk, our save-or-waste game, and your poster or promise. Step two. Be honest. This is not a test, and there are no marks. If something is not quite there yet, choose that! Saying "not yet" is brave and helpful. It shows your teacher where to help you next. I expect honest answers, not all happy faces just to look good. Step three. Now look at the bottom of the page. There is a deck of slides, with one sentence on each slide. Press Start. Read the sentence, choose your answer, then press the arrow to go to the next one. Keep going, one slide at a time. On the very last slide, press the finish button. Take your time — there is no rush. Step four. When every sentence has an answer, press I have finished reflecting at the bottom of the page. Only press it when nothing is left blank. That button saves your work, so it must come from you. You will know the page is finished when the sentences all have answers, the slide deck is finished, and you have pressed I have finished reflecting. Now, one little question from me before you begin: what is one way you can save water at home? 💧
